pipeline.name: GitHub Issue Triage
pipeline.description: Pick the most sensible open GitHub issue, enrich it with PRD context from docs/PRD.md, and create a feature/issue-N branch. Implementation stays on the new branch for IDE / claude-code.

tpl_triage_fetch.name: GH Issue Fetcher
tpl_triage_fetch.prompt_template:
<agent_prompt version="1">
  <role>{{ role }}</role>
  <command>set -e
ISSUES=$(gh issue list --state open --limit 50 --json number,title,body,labels,updatedAt)
printf '<output>{"available_issues": %s}</output>\n' "$ISSUES"</command>
</agent_prompt>

tpl_triage_select.name: Issue Selector
tpl_triage_select.prompt_template:
<agent_prompt version="1">
  <role>{{ role }}</role>
  <task>
    From the "available_issues" list, pick exactly ONE issue that makes the most sense to work on now.
    Rank by, in order:
      1. Priority (labels like "high" / "critical" win)
      2. Small surface area + clear scope (issue can be finished in one iteration)
      3. Recency — recently updated issues take priority
      4. No dependency on other open work

    Return ONLY in the <output> block:
      - selected_issue_ids: a single-element list containing the chosen issue number
  </task>
  <available_issues>{{ available_issues | tojson }}</available_issues>
  <constraints>
    Always pick exactly one. If the list is empty, return selected_issue_ids: [].
  </constraints>
</agent_prompt>

tpl_triage_load_prd.name: PRD Loader
tpl_triage_load_prd.prompt_template:
<agent_prompt version="1">
  <role>{{ role }}</role>
  <command>set -e
if [ -f docs/PRD.md ]; then
  PRD=$(cat docs/PRD.md | jq -Rs .)
else
  PRD='"(no docs/PRD.md found in working directory)"'
fi
printf '<output>{"implementation_notes": %s}</output>\n' "$PRD"</command>
</agent_prompt>

tpl_triage_enrich.name: Issue Enricher
tpl_triage_enrich.prompt_template:
<agent_prompt version="1">
  <role>{{ role }}</role>
  <task>
    Build a complete briefing for a developer / test_author working on the selected issue.

    You have:
      - "implementation_notes" — contains the raw PRD loaded from docs/PRD.md by the previous node.
      - "selected_issue_ids" — number of the chosen issue.
      - "available_issues" — full list (reference, e.g. for related-issue links).

    Find the matching issue in available_issues (by number = selected_issue_ids[0]).
    Overwrite implementation_notes with this structure:

      # Issue #{number}: {title}

      ## Goal
      What the user gets when this issue is closed (1-2 sentences).

      ## Context from PRD
      Quote the relevant sections. If the PRD does not cover this area, say "PRD does not cover this" and propose follow-up questions.

      ## Acceptance criteria
      Bullet list of measurable conditions.

      ## Suggested tests
      Concrete scenarios (3-5) that would be enough to validate the change.

      ## Related issues
      Issue numbers from available_issues that block / depend / duplicate this one.

      ## Risks / open questions
      What is uncertain and needs a decision.

    Return ONLY in the <output> block: implementation_notes with the structure above as a single string.
  </task>
  <selected_issue_ids>{{ selected_issue_ids }}</selected_issue_ids>
  <implementation_notes>{{ implementation_notes }}</implementation_notes>
  <available_issues>{{ available_issues | tojson }}</available_issues>
</agent_prompt>

tpl_triage_branch.name: Branch Creator
tpl_triage_branch.prompt_template:
<agent_prompt version="1">
  <role>{{ role }}</role>
  <command>set -e
ISSUE={{ selected_issue_ids[0] }}
git fetch origin
git checkout -B "feature/issue-$ISSUE" origin/main
printf '<output>{"branch": "feature/issue-%s"}</output>\n' "$ISSUE"</command>
</agent_prompt>
